search_protocol.date_filter: newly published or newly available after 2026-11-07 through 2026-11-13
search_protocol.inclusion: Original scientific paper or authoritative research report with a primary DOI/publisher record and enough verified methods/results to assess relevance and limitations.
search_protocol.exclusion: News-only items, work outside the incremental window, reviews without directly useful new evidence, and papers too indirect for Jubilee forecasting.
search_protocol.verification: Each inclusion was checked twice: the primary publisher/full-text or DOI-indexed article record, plus a separate publisher-index, preprint metadata, or bibliographic read.

publications.title: Hydrodynamic controls of hypoxia formation in a shallow inverse estuary: Insights from Kuwait Bay
publications.publication_date_note: Online publication date observed in the bounded 2026-11-12 search; publisher DOI and volume records were rechecked on 2026-11-13.

observational_coverage.system: Kuwait Bay, a shallow inverse estuary in the north Arabian/Persian Gulf
observational_coverage.current_analysis: Empirical orthogonal function analysis of near-bed current velocities

publications.methods: The accessible accepted-article abstract and publisher highlights describe in-situ environmental observations at one near-bed station and EOF decomposition of subtidal currents. Two modes explained about 92% of current variability: an east-west advective mode (about 78%) and a vertically sheared bidirectional mode (about 14%).
findings: The bidirectional circulation mode was associated with trapping low-oxygen water and prolonging event duration.
Publisher highlights report that Shamal wind forcing led near-bed dissolved oxygen by roughly 2–4 days, which the authors present as a candidate early-warning relationship.
The paper links hypoxia persistence to transport and retention dynamics rather than oxygen loading alone and explicitly situates the system in a history of summer hypoxia and fish kills.
publications.evidence_quality: High relevance to transport/ventilation hypotheses, but limited observational breadth: one station and two events. The accepted article is peer reviewed; this review did not treat peer review as independent validation.
uncertainty_and_limitations: Accepted full text could not be independently extracted in this run; findings above are limited to the DOI-indexed abstract, publisher highlights and prior-preprint indexed text.
No multi-station spatial validation, external estuary validation, held-out forecast evaluation, calibration analysis or Jubilee biological endpoint was verified.
Kuwait Bay is hypersaline/inverse and climatically distinct from Mobile Bay; the sign and lag of wind-current-oxygen relationships are not directly transferable.
A two-event lead relationship is exploratory and cannot support a production feature or threshold.
mobile_bay_implications: Offline only: test whether observed/local near-bed transport modes and wind-to-oxygen lags add event-blocked value after direct Eastern Shore current and bottom-oxygen gates are cleared.
Treat retention/bidirectional flow as a state interaction, not a standalone monotonic predictor.
Do not reopen the deferred wind-capture optimization project; this is a scientific transport hypothesis, not evidence for camera reduction.
offline_validation_opportunities: On retained event/control windows, compare transport-only versus oxygen-loading-only and combined models with time-blocked evaluation.
Require local current geometry, depth, units, clock/timezone and direct bottom-oxygen provenance before testing the reported 2–4 day lead.
Estimate uncertainty across events and reject the feature if the lag or sign is unstable.

publications.title: Transitional ecosystem states in coastal waters undergoing changing oxygen conditions revealed by coupled geochemical and microbial dynamics
institutions: Centre for Ecology and Evolution in Microbial Model Systems, Linnaeus University
Department of Ecology, Environment and Plant Sciences, Stockholm University
Centre for the Environment, Linnaeus University

observational_coverage.system: Coastal Baltic Sea bay near Loftahammar, Sweden
observational_coverage.replication: Three biological replicate sediment cores per site/date
observational_coverage.measurements: surface-sediment and water geochemistry, in-situ surface/bottom oxygen/temperature/salinity/pH, 16S rRNA amplicons, metatranscriptomics

publications.methods: Repeated sampling across one year at three depth/oxygen-history sites; combined sediment biogeochemistry, 16S rRNA community profiling and metatranscriptomic activity analysis. The public data/code references include NCBI BioProjects and a GitHub analysis repository.
findings: Long-term oxygen history was the primary structuring factor for microbial community composition and transcriptional profiles.

The shallow mostly oxic and deep long-term low-oxygen sites were comparatively stable, while the intermediate fluctuating-oxygen site had the greatest temporal variability and stronger transcriptional shifts.
The authors interpret transitional oxygen habitats as dynamic ecological states responsive to environmental variability.
publications.evidence_quality: Strong mechanistic and provenance value for sediment-state persistence, with full methods/data references, but it is a single Baltic bay, one sampling year and a microbial/sediment endpoint rather than a forecast or fish-event study.
uncertainty_and_limitations: No external or out-of-sample validation and no operational forecast evaluation.
Only three sites; depth and long-term oxygen regime are partly confounded.
Sampling was periodic rather than continuous and some oxygen/geochemistry entries were missing.
Baltic depths, salinity, seasonality and sediment ecology differ materially from Mobile Bay.
Microbial/transcriptomic state is not a Jubilee label and is not available as a pre-event production input.
mobile_bay_implications: Offline only: assess whether retained antecedent bottom-oxygen and sediment/organic-matter proxies exhibit regime persistence or nonlinear transition behavior.
Prefer state-space or persistence features over treating each low-oxygen observation as independent, but require local dated events and matched controls.
Do not infer biological detection, fish aggregation or production benefit from sediment microbial shifts.
offline_validation_opportunities: When reliable local bottom-oxygen sequences exist, compare memory/state-transition features with same-day oxygen-loading baselines under event-blocked validation.
Test whether intermediate/fluctuating regimes are associated with greater error or event probability, with uncertainty and site effects explicit.
Reject the hypothesis if it does not improve Brier/log loss and decision utility on held-out Jubilee event/control windows.

exclusions.title: Increased Hydrological Connectivity Does Not Always Lead to Increased Nutrient Removal Potential in a Coastal River Delta
exclusions.reason: Substantive original delta nutrient-transport study, but no directly verified dissolved-oxygen, hypoxia or fish-event endpoint; excluded rather than padding the quota.

exclusions.title: Integrated transcriptomic and metabolomic profiling of hypoxia response in a marine bivalve
exclusions.reason: Organismal laboratory-response work with weaker direct relevance to Mobile Bay event forecasting than the two included studies; excluded without padding.

exclusions.title: Spatiotemporal extent of diel and episodic hypoxia in bottom water of a shallow, well-mixed estuary
exclusions.reason: Highly relevant but published 2026-08-31 and therefore outside the incremental post-2026-11-07 window; retained as an out-of-window candidate rather than presented as new.

synthesis.new_scientific_finding: Two post-window original studies reinforce separate transport-retention and oxygen-history/state-memory hypotheses, but neither validates a Mobile Bay Jubilee forecast or biological detection endpoint.
research_questions: Do locally observed near-bed transport/retention states add held-out value beyond oxygen-loading features once current/geometry and bottom-oxygen gates are cleared?
Do antecedent low-oxygen histories create measurable state persistence or transition risk in dated Jubilee event/control windows?
next_steps: Reuse these two hypotheses only in bounded offline time-blocked tests after reliable local inputs and matched controls exist.
Continue compact-JSON biological equivalence and actual billed-cost acceptance ahead of wind-capture optimization.
unresolved_risks: No positive-event paired compact/original biological challenge set.
No validated local near-bed current geometry or direct Eastern Shore bottom-oxygen time series.
